info.name: VELOCITY-AI — API Resources
info.description: Full backend API surface organized strictly by resource — one folder per API resource, one request per route (plus the Hello HTML (E2E) folder driving the local hello_html test workflow end to end). Generated 1:1 from backend/app/api (93 REST routes + /ws/handoff WebSocket, documented as a placeholder request since collection v2.1 cannot express WS). Import the environment at tools/api/postman/VELOCITY-AI-Local.postman_environment.json (or the copy next to this file) and run Auth > POST /api/auth/login first — its test script captures {{jwt}} for the collection-level Bearer auth.

request.description: Creates a new user (basic tier by default). Not idempotent — re-running with the same email 409s once the user exists; that's expected.
Captures {{jwt}} into a collection variable (shared collection-wide via the collection-level Bearer auth) — safe to re-run from any folder.
Returns the authenticated user's profile (id/email/tier/is_admin) for the {{jwt}} bearer token.
Revokes the current {{jwt}}. Run last — subsequent authenticated requests in this collection will 401 until you log in again.
Requires an admin-tier {{jwt}} — log in as an admin account first.

Same route as the concrete `Pipelines — <name>` requests above (`/api/agents/pipelines/{pipeline_type}`), parametrized so any current or future `pipeline_type` value can be exercised without adding a new request.
Lists the CALLING USER's own saved per-agent skill overrides only — not a global catalog.
Response id can be captured into {{chatId}} via a test script, same pattern as Login → {{jwt}}.
Called by the flowin-handoff CLI installer/script, not typically by the FE. Captures a token you can put in {{handoffToken}} for the two requests below.

WebSocket route, not REST — this placeholder only documents it. Connect with Postman's 'New > WebSocket Request' to ws://<apiRoot host>/ws/handoff/{{handoffToken}}. Do not send this as an HTTP request.
Lists the hook library available to the authenticated user.

od-ppt-brief-analyst / od-ppt-composer declare template injection -- the Launch step below needs a real template_id (chosen from this list) or it fails immediately with "missing_template_context". This is the theme-selection step.
Same route as 'Template detail — saas-landing' above, parametrized.
Note: "linear" (used elsewhere in this repo) is stale -- the real id is "linear-app". This is the theme-selection step.
Distinct from the Runs > Prototype (od_prototype) pipeline flow above — this is the standalone synchronous prototype-generation endpoint.

agent_ids must keep the full dependency chain intact -- dropping nfr-specialist/backlog-reviewer 422s with "workflow_unsatisfiable" since backlog-compiler consumes their outputs (found via live testing).

body.raw:
{
  "pipeline_type": "user_stories",
  "message": "Build a backlog for a personal finance budgeting app, informed by a quick competitive scan first.",
  "agent_ids": [
    "domain-analyst",
    "market-research-agent",
    "epic-architect",
    "story-estimator",
    "nfr-specialist",
    "backlog-reviewer",
    "backlog-compiler"
  ]
}

request.description: Always fails with "Could not find PptxGenJS code" for od_ppt runs -- export-pptx only works for pipelines with a ppt-code-generator agent, which od_ppt does not have.
Set {{runId}} to the run you want to inspect.
Run LAST if you use this — deletes whatever {{runId}} currently points at.
Distinct from the live SSE stream above — a plain GET returning the durable event log so far. Useful to confirm what actually happened even if a Watch request above timed out.

Attaches to the live stream right after launch. Every pipeline here has clarify.mode: auto, so it ALWAYS pauses at questionnaire_ready (after workflow_validated -> planner_start -> planner_complete -> gate_status) before any agent runs. This request stays open/blocked until you stop it -- verified live that answering too early (before this pause is actually armed) is silently dropped, so you must let this request reach questionnaire_ready first. In the Postman app: watch it arrive, then cancel this request and move to the next one. Running via Newman: pass --timeout-request 10000 (or similar) so it's aborted automatically once the pause has had time to arm -- that's expected, not a bug.
Only send this if part 2's stream paused on a review_gate_ready event (Human_Gate agents) instead of reaching a terminal event.

Send this only AFTER questionnaire_ready has actually arrived on the stream above (or after that request's timeout, which gives it enough time to arm) -- answering earlier is silently dropped, verified live.
Uses {{runId}} — set it to the run you want to inspect.
One up-channel chat turn to a LIVE run. message_id is the idempotency key ({{$guid}} generates a fresh one per send — resending the same id is a no-op).
Chains a child revision run off {{runId}} — send this AFTER the run above has completed.
Lists the skill library available to the authenticated user.
Dynamic, manifest-driven catalog (FIX-051/ISS-035) — every launchable pipeline with its id/name/step_count/steps.
Full compiled step detail (planner, clarify_mode, deliverable, per-step strategy/gates/validators) for one workflow id.

item.name: Hello HTML (E2E)

request.description: Captures {{jwt}} into a collection variable (shared collection-wide via the collection-level Bearer auth) — safe to re-run from any folder.
Sanity-check the compiled hello_html definition: 3 steps (emoji-picker → writer[human gate] → presenter[html_static validator]), deliverable page.html.
The three discovered agents with their orders and the writer's Human_Gate.

Launches hello_html. The word for the run comes from the emoji-picker's random_word tool call (watch for it in the stream's tool_call events); the message is just the brief. The test script captures {{runId}}.

SSE leg: keep it open and watch the event stream until `questionnaire_ready` arrives, then cancel this request and continue with the next step. Acting before the event has actually arrived is silently dropped.

Send this only AFTER questionnaire_ready has actually arrived on the stream above (or after that request's timeout, which gives it enough time to arm) -- answering earlier is silently dropped, verified live.
Chat with the run while it executes — one up-channel turn; message_id ({{$guid}}) is the idempotency key. Watch the stream leg for the reply.

SSE leg: keep it open and watch the event stream until `review_gate_ready` arrives, then cancel this request and continue with the next step. Acting before the event has actually arrived is silently dropped.
Resolves the writer step's human gate. Paste the gate_key from the review_gate_ready event seen on the stream leg above. Use action reject/redo to exercise the other paths.

SSE leg: keep it open and watch the event stream until `run completion (workflow_complete)` arrives, then cancel this request and continue with the next step. Acting before the event has actually arrived is silently dropped.
Set {{runId}} to the run you want to inspect.
Distinct from the live SSE stream above — a plain GET returning the durable event log so far. Useful to confirm what actually happened even if a Watch request above timed out.

item.description: End-to-end test flow for the LOCAL hello_html workflow (copy of deep_agents hello-html: emoji-picker → writer → presenter, deliverable page.html). Run top to bottom: launch with one word, answer the clarify questionnaire after questionnaire_ready, chat with the run mid-flight, approve the writer's human gate after review_gate_ready, then inspect status/events/artifacts. Requires the backend restarted with the hello_html manifest + agents on disk (uncommitted local test files).
